lines.text: "Restock in three. Two. One."
"Restock in three. Two. One."
Step one: make a list. Every part in a tab. Twenty-nineteen. It's fun.
Step two: add it up. Twelve hundred. Save eight. Four to go. You're nearly done.
Step three: wait for March. The tax return. The card. The build. The game. The one.
Step four: refresh the page. It's a Tuesday. It's in stock. It's on sale. Don't blink.
Step five: blink. A building bought them. Forty thousand at a time. Think
About what a building does with forty thousand cards. It thinks. It's a building that thinks.
Step six: check the RAM. Sixteen gigs of the old kind. Forty dollars last year. A hundred and twenty. Sure.
Step seven: check the drive. A terabyte. Forty-five. Ninety now. The phones are shrinking on the inside to endure.
Step eight: check the case. It's fine. It's a box. It's the one part they don't want. It's on the floor. It's yours. It's pure.
Step nine: do the math. It's not a number. It's a chart. It's a weather report. It's a tab you keep.
Step ten: close the tab. Open it. Close it. It's a hobby now. The hobby's the tab. The tab's the rig. You don't sleep.
Step eleven: read the news. Three companies make all the memory on earth. Nine-tenths to the buildings. Three years signed. It's deep.
Out of stock, or out of stock for me?
Before it was made, who signed three years of memory?
Where does a wafer go when it leaves the fab, and who did it leave?
"It's compute for us! No compute for thee!"
Step twelve: press "notify me." It's free. It's a button. It's a prayer with a bell.
Step thirteen: a podcast. "Compute is the new oil," says a man who has never seen a well.
Step fourteen: read the CEO. "We're grateful to the gaming community. Enterprise is now our target. Also, thanks for the jacket!"
Step fifteen: a bot buys nine in the second it takes your thumb to move, then sells you one at triple. That's the racket.
Step sixteen: "Just buy last gen," says a man with this gen, on a stream, in a ring light, to a cam.
Step seventeen: last gen's a used card from a mine that ran hot for two years, and last gen's price went up too. Even the RAM.
Step eighteen: ask when it ends. One store says "twenty-twenty-eight." The other says "past twenty-thirty." Take your pick.
Step nineteen: this manual was written in twenty-twenty-six, so every number in it is already wrong. Read it quick.
Out of stock, or out of stock for me?
Before it was made, who signed three years of memory?
Where does a wafer go when it leaves the fab, and who did it leave?
"It's compute for us! No compute for thee!"
Step twenty: ask for one card. "Ask for a quote. Quotes are available."
Step twenty-one: say "one card, one person." "Minimum order five hundred. Business accounts are available."
Step twenty-two: offer eight hundred dollars. "That's a month of the cloud. Hourly is available."
Step twenty-three: say "I wanted to build it." "Profiles are available. Workflows are available. The browser is available."
Step twenty-four: ask where the card is. "In a building, in a state with cheap water, at scale. Scale is available."
Step twenty-five: look at the case on the floor by the desk with nothing in it. Three years. You still call it the build.
Step twenty-six: say yes to the cloud. Say yes to the annual plan. Say yes to being billed. You're billed. Billing is available.
Step twenty-seven: there is no step twenty-seven. Nothing is available.
Out of stock, or out of stock for me?
Before it was made, who signed three years of memory?
Where does a wafer go when it leaves the fab, and who did it leave?
"It's compute for us! No compute for thee!"
"Restock in three. Two. One."
"Restock in three, two, one."
"Restock in three two one."
"Restockinthreetwoone."
